title: A Giant Tortoise Was Filmed Hunting a Baby Bird. It Took 7 Minutes

scenes.text: The slowest hunt ever filmed still ended with a kill.
July 2020, an island in the Seychelles. A giant tortoise, an animal that lives on leaves, walks straight at a tern chick sitting on a log.
Her jaws are open, her tongue pulled back. The chick backs away along the log. She keeps coming.
The chick could drop to the ground and get away. It won't. Terns nest in trees, and a chick's instinct says the ground is the danger.
After seven minutes it runs out of log. One bite to the head, and she swallows it whole.
It's the first deliberate hunt ever recorded in a wild tortoise. Scientists say she looked like she'd done it before, and others on the island do it too.

description:
A giant tortoise was filmed hunting, killing and eating a baby bird.
In July 2020 on Fregate Island in the Seychelles, conservation manager Anna Zora filmed a female giant tortoise pursuing a lesser noddy tern chick along a log for seven minutes, biting its head and swallowing it whole. Published in Current Biology in August 2021 with Justin Gerlach of the University of Cambridge, it is the first documented deliberate hunting by any wild tortoise; the island has about 3,000 tortoises and a colony of 265,000 noddy terns, and other tortoises there have been seen making similar attacks.
Did you think tortoises only ate plants?
subject: giant tortoise
first_comment: The Cambridge scientist who studied the film said she seemed to know what she was doing. Would you have guessed a tortoise could hunt?
